newsitem.title: USA: TIAA-CREF plans to tap into new markets - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: TIAA-CREF plans to tap into new markets - WSJ.

text.p: Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association-College Retirement Equities Fund -- the largest U.S. pension fund, known as TIAA-CREF -- plans to tap into new markets now that it has been stripped of its tax-exempt status by Washington, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
The newspaper said in its electronic edition that TIAA-CREF's president and chief executive, Thomas Jones, said those new markets include state-run pension funds for teachers.

He also said the fund system would seek to offer retirement investments to college employees' families and to hospital workers who had been members of TIAA-CREF when they worked at teaching hospitals, according to the paper.
The loss of the exemption under the recent federal-tax overhaul may cost TIAA-CREF as much as $1.2 billion over the next several years, the paper said, citing a TIAA-CREF spokeswoman.
